summary: The provisioning half of running the platform: single-use, time-limited invites that name the kind of account they create, the instance's account list, account removal under a last-administrator guard, an administrator's own password rotation, and the bootstrap CLI.

read.role: the request gate that refuses every /api/admin/ request before any handler runs, at the status the Refusals table gives, the error page a refused /admin navigation shows, and the administrator's stripped chrome. Its refusal fingerprint matrix is where the admin routes' refusals are matched
the consumer of an invite and the writer of the kind it names
the rule that writes last_login_at, which GET /api/admin/accounts reports as lastLoginAt
the shared change-password endpoint an administrator reaches, and the vault owner deletion path this one is not
the other administrator task on this surface, owned there and not here
the administrator's frame, the section switcher that replaces nav inside the admin area, the dialog and table conventions, and the phone-width sizes
the administration surface this feature drives

inviteKind.value: vault_owner or administrator, chosen at creation and never edited. It is the sole source of the kind of the account the invite produces

inviteToken.value: 256 bits from secrets.token_urlsafe(32), shown once at creation in the response and never retrievable afterwards

inviteTokenHashing.value: SHA-256. The token is high-entropy and unguessable, so a slow KDF buys nothing. Lookup is by hash, in constant time, never by scanning and comparing plaintext

inviteExpiry.value: default 7 days, set by the administrator at creation within 1 to 30 days

inviteStatus.value: pending, then used or revoked. expired is derived from expires_at and not stored, so it cannot drift

singleUse.value: consumed atomically in the same transaction as the account insert. A failed registration does not consume it

createdBy.value: the administrator who minted the invite, or the reserved sentinel system:bootstrap for one minted by the CLI. Stored and never returned: GET /api/admin/invites leaves it out and no screen shows it. The sentinel is refused as a username at registration

createInvite.value: POST /api/admin/invites { expiresInDays, label, kind } returning { id, token, url, expiresAt, kind }. kind is required and has no default, and any other value is a Bad Request. The only response that ever contains the token

listInvites.value: GET /api/admin/invites returning { id, label, kind, createdAt, expiresAt, status, usedAt, usedBy }. Never includes the token or its hash

revokeInvite.value: POST /api/admin/invites/<id>/revoke sets status revoked. Idempotent on an already-revoked invite, refused on a used one

listAccounts.value: GET /api/admin/accounts returning per account { username, kind, createdAt, lastLoginAt }, plus recordCount for a vault owner only. A union discriminated on kind, and recordCount is absent for an administrator rather than zero. Both kinds are listed

deleteAccount.value: DELETE /api/admin/accounts/<username> { confirmUsername } deletes that principal's row, its credential, its wrapper, every record and every session in one transaction. Keyed by normalized username, and confirmUsername must equal the path segment or the request is a Bad Request

lastLoginAtNeverNull.value: lastLoginAt is a timestamp on every row of GET /api/admin/accounts and never null, because registration is a sign-in. A new account's lastLoginAt equals its createdAt, and a later sign-in moves it past createdAt without touching any other row's. A principals row whose last_login_at is null in the file before the app starts returns its createdAt as lastLoginAt, by the start-up backfill

adminEndpointAccess.value: every path under /api/admin/, named in this file or not, is refused to anyone but an administrator as an invented /api/ path is. The request gate refuses an administrator session every vault route

noKindChangeAnywhere.value: there is no endpoint that changes an account's kind, no promote, no demote, and no field on any request that is read into principals.kind after the insert

adminBoundary.value: no endpoint returns any record ciphertext, any field of any account's credential row meaning salt, KDF envelope or Auth Key hash, or any wrapper. An administrator cannot reset a password and holds no destructive power beyond removing an account outright. The same person's two accounts are not linked anywhere and no feature may add a link

lastAdministratorGuard.value: at least one administrator account exists at all times. A deletion that would leave none is refused with Conflict. The guard and the delete are one BEGIN IMMEDIATE transaction, so two administrators removing each other concurrently cannot both succeed. There is no guard on removing the last vault owner

whoMayRemoveWhom.value: an administrator may remove any account of either kind including another administrator and including their own, while another administrator remains, which ends their own session with the transaction. An administrator's own account is removed here and nowhere else

administratorPasswordChange.value: one control in the admin area posting to POST /api/auth/change-password, the same shared endpoint a vault owner uses, sending no wrapper. It invalidates every other session of that administrator and keeps the current one, which is also the administrator's sign out everywhere. There is no session list for an administrator and no POST /api/auth/logout-all

forgottenAdministratorPassword.value: an administrator who has forgotten their password is not recovered, they are replaced. There is deliberately no power for one administrator to reset another's password

bootstrapCli.value: flask create-invite --kind administrator --expires-days 1. --kind is required and takes administrator or vault-owner. It prints an invite URL and exits, creating an invite and never an account. --force is required whenever an administrator account already exists, and without it the command refuses, exits non-zero and prints how many accounts of each kind there are plus the flag that would proceed

inviteUrl.value: https://<host>/register?invite=<token>, copied to the clipboard and delivered out of band. The app does not email it

referrerPolicy.value: Referrer-Policy: no-referrer on /register and on admin UI pages. The register page is the one that matters, because the token rides in its URL

tokenDroppedFromAddressBar.value: the register page drops the token with history.replaceState once the form has taken it, and the form submits the token it already holds rather than the URL's copy

tokenNotLogged.value: the token must not appear in the application's own log output. The deployment's reverse proxy or tunnel logging is documented as a place it may still appear

vaultOwnerOnAdminRoute.condition: an /api/admin/ request with the header and a vault owner session, refused as an invented /api/ path is (spec/features/admin-invites.md#edge-cases, spec/architecture.md#refusals)

noSessionOnAdminRoute.condition: an /api/admin/ request with the header and no valid session, refused as an invented /api/ path is (spec/features/admin-invites.md#endpoints)

noHeaderOnAdminRoute.condition: an /api/admin/ request without X-Solvent-Request, whether or not the path exists and whatever the session

revokeUsedInvite.condition: a used invite cannot be revoked, and the message points at account deletion instead (spec/features/admin-invites.md#edge-cases)

lastAdministratorRemoval.condition: a deletion that would leave no administrator (spec/features/admin-invites.md#who-may-remove-whom-and-the-last-administrator)

confirmUsernameMismatch.condition: confirmUsername does not equal the path segment (spec/features/admin-invites.md#endpoints)

createInviteWithoutKind.condition: kind is required and has no default (spec/features/admin-invites.md#endpoints)

removingAnUnknownUsername.condition: identical to the refusal of an invented /api/ path (spec/features/admin-invites.md#edge-cases)

fixtures: a route enumerator over the registered routes under /api/admin/ read at test time rather than a fixed list, which is what makes the boundary test cover an endpoint added later
three seeded administrators and two populated vault owners, for the removal, the last-administrator guard and the untouched-other-account assertions
two overlapping DELETE /api/admin/accounts requests, each targeting one of the only two administrators, issued concurrently rather than serially
an invite in each of the four bad states, invalid, expired, used and revoked, sharing the registration-error assertion with register
a CLI-minted invite, for the system:bootstrap sentinel and the refused-username assertion
a fresh instance with no administrator and an instance with one, for the CLI's two behaviours and the --force override
a fault injected mid-delete, for the target account being fully intact and able to sign in afterwards
captured application log output over an invite creation and a registration, for the token-absence assertion
a vault owner session and an invented /api/ path as the comparison baseline, for the admin-route refusal
a real browser opening /admin signed out and as a vault owner next to an invented page path, for the page a refused admin address shows (app-shell.md owns the page and its assertions)

a first administrator registered through a flask create-invite invite, then a vault owner and a second administrator registered through in-app invites, for the lastLoginAt-equals-createdAt assertion over every row
a stubbed server clock that can advance before one account's sign-in, for the lastLoginAt-moves-for-that-row-only assertion
a SQLite file holding a principals row with a null last_login_at before the app starts, for the backfilled lastLoginAt assertion
focus: every registered /api/admin/ route, enumerated at test time under every method it answers, must be refused to a vault owner as an invented /api/ path is, not just the routes that look likely. A status check alone would pass a route that still answers Method Not Allowed, a redirect or Forbidden through a different header. The match on body and headers is app-shell.md's refusal fingerprint matrix

the no-session case is Unauthorized only with the header present, and a request without it is Forbidden whatever the session (architecture.md, Refusals). A test that sends the header on every call never shows which of the two the gate picks, and a test that omits it never shows the 401

no endpoint under /api/admin/ may return any record ciphertext, any field of any account's credential row or any wrapper. This is the executable form of the admin boundary and it has to enumerate the registered routes at test time and inspect each one's full response shape, so an endpoint added later is tested automatically instead of needing to be added to a list. A fixed list of routes passes forever and misses the one that crosses the line
the same enumeration has to be used for the no-kind-change rule, attempting the change through every registered route rather than through the ones that look likely

the last-administrator guard must be tested with two genuinely overlapping requests. The serial case passes whether or not the count and the delete share a transaction, and the concurrent case is the bug the BEGIN IMMEDIATE exists for
recordCount must be shown to be absent for an administrator by asserting against the row's full key set, not against its value. A zero passes any value-based check and says exactly the wrong thing
the four bad-invite refusals must be byte-identical, which is shared with register and easy to leave half-asserted on one side
the token must be shown to appear in no table and in no application log line, over captured output from a real creation and registration rather than a source grep

every control in the rendered admin area must map to a route under /api/admin/ or to POST /api/auth/change-password, asserted against the rendered area, so a control wired to a vault route fails whatever it is for

lastLoginAt must be asserted on every row at two moments, right after the first administrator registers and again after a vault owner and a second administrator register, with each equal to its createdAt, and then after one account signs in with the clock advanced, with only that row moved. The backfilled row needs the file pre-written before start-up. A check on the administrator row alone, or on a fresh database alone, passes while a null leaks through
an administrator removing their own account while another remains must be shown to end their own session, not merely to return a success status
a mid-delete failure must leave the target account able to sign in, asserted by actually signing in rather than by reading rows
